public_rationale: Zitron says nobody can measure the ROI of AI or set a standard per-task cost, because LLMs hallucinate and harnesses keep multiplying. Read fairly, this means a cross-tool, predictable cost standard, not one vendor's average. But the claim is an impossibility thesis tied to a cause. Whether anyone 'can actually' measure ROI depends on what counts as a valid measurement, and he gives no test. Company ROI surveys or vendor cost-per-task figures, like Anthropic's own reported cut, would not settle it, because he could fairly say they are not the standard he means. The cause he names cannot be separated from other reasons a standard is missing. So the claim cannot be fairly graded true or false.
limitations: I did not survey academic ROI-measurement literature in depth, because no single study could settle an impossibility claim with an undefined standard.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Nobody can measure the ROI of AI or standardize the cost of a task, because LLMs inherently hallucinate and harnesses and interfaces keep multiplying.

statement.excerpt: That’s because, as I’ve said before, nobody can actually measure the ROI of AI, or even create a standard measurement of the cost of a task thanks to the inevitable hallucination-prone nature of LLMs and the ever-growing list of different harnesses and “agentic” (sigh) interfaces.

our_interpretation: In context, 'standard measurement of the cost of a task' means a per-task cost that holds across tools and harnesses and can be predicted in advance. It does not mean any one vendor's or benchmark's average.
'Nobody can actually measure the ROI of AI' is an impossibility claim. It turns on what counts as a real ROI measurement, and the speaker gives no test for that.
The 'thanks to' clause gives a cause (hallucination and harness sprawl). No public evidence could isolate that cause from other reasons a standard is missing.
criteria.support_condition: Would be supported if there were no credible, accepted method for measuring AI ROI and no cross-harness standard for per-task cost, and if that gap could be shown to come from hallucination and harness sprawl.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Would be contradicted by a widely adopted, reproducible method for measuring AI ROI or a standard per-task cost that holds across harnesses and can be predicted.

evidence.locator: paragraph after the 'Where Anthropic's Compute Goes' table
evidence.explanation: A vendor reports its own cost-per-task changes. This shows that company-specific task-cost metrics exist. It is not a standard that holds across harnesses, which is what the claim is about, so it does not settle the claim.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An industry-wide, cross-harness standard for per-task AI cost, or an accepted ROI method, would let the claim be tested. So would a clear definition of what the speaker counts as a valid measurement.
